messages:
Jenna (ACME): Hey, hitting a bunch of failures in JSON mode when we upgraded SDK 2.8 -> 3.0. The model keeps returning quoted numbers and some enum values with wrong casing, which breaks our validator (TypeError: expected number). request-id: req_0a9f.

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal request + response? which model and are you using `strict_json`? :eyes:

Jenna (ACME): Using `gptx-1.2` through the hosted API, sending `structured_output: { mode: "json_schema", schema_version: 2 }` and `strict_json: true`. Example payload:

```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "structured_output": {
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "invoice_id": {"type": "number"},
        "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["PAID","PENDING","FAILED"]},
        "paid": {"type": "boolean"}
      },
      "required": ["invoice_id","status","paid"]
    },
    "mode": "json_schema",
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

Response body (what we got):

```
{
  "invoice_id": "12345",
  "status": "Paid",
  "paid": null
}
```

This trips our JSON schema validator: `expected number but got string` and `enum mismatch: "Paid" not in ["PAID","PENDING","FAILED"]`. Also `paid` becomes null instead of `false`.

alex_support: Thanks, that clarifies. Two separate issues: 1) numeric values quoted (string vs number), 2) enum casing + null for bool. Quick Qs: does the problem happen reproducibly on every attempt? can you share the full curl with headers (api key redacted)?

Jenna (ACME): Yes reproducible, here's sanitized curl + request-id header: `x-rdwd-request-id: req_0a9f`.

alex_support: Reproduced locally against same model/version. Getting the same output. Adding eng-ml. @maria_ml — possible regression in the JSON formatter/strict parser after SDK bump?

maria_ml: looking. Initial hypothesis: the formatter enforces JSON blocks but we had a recent change that prefers lexical quoting for numerics in some sampling seeds, which can produce quoted numbers. Also there's an enum normalization pass that used to uppercase enums but a refactor may have made it case-preserving and allowed `null` to fill missing booleans under `strict`.

luis_oncall: Can you dump the server-side parse trace for `req_0a9f`? I'll check model logits and post-process stage.

ingest-bot: Trace uploaded -> https://internal/redwood/traces/req_0a9f (team only).

maria_ml: I reviewed the trace: the model output tokens contained "12345" (i.e., digits wrapped in quotes) for that slot. Post-process attempted to coerce types but in `strict=true` mode coercion is disabled and instead we return as-is with an error. The enum pipeline had a normalization toggle off, so `Paid` didn't map to `PAID`. The `paid` boolean token was `null` because the model generated the token `null` for that slot.

alex_support: Mitigation options for ACME: a) set `strict=false` (temporary) which enables permissive coercion and enum normalization; b) add a lightweight pre-parse pass in our proxy to coerce quoted digits to numbers for required numeric fields; c) update prompt to explicitly say: `Output numbers without quotes and booleans as true/false` while we push a fix. Which would you prefer?

Jenna (ACME): We need a short-term fix that doesn't change our validator. Option b sounds safest — can you flip the per-tenant proxy rule? We're on Dedicated so per-tenant change is fine.

maria_ml: I can prioritize a short patch: in the parsing layer, if `strict=true` and schema expects `number`, still allow string->number coercion when the string matches `^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$` and log a warning. Will open a PR with tests.

luis_oncall: I'll roll a canary to staging and run ACME's repro suite. ETA ~2 hours for canary, 6 hours for full rollout if green.

alex_support: Jenna — temporary proxy rule applied (allow_string_numbers=true) for your tenant. Please re-run tests and paste results. :rocket:

Jenna (ACME): Running now... all green. validator accepts invoice_id as number now. status normalized to `PAID` too? I still see `Paid` in one case.

alex_support: Hmm, enum normalization not fixed yet. maria, can we add case-insensitive enum matching in the normalization pass for the patch?

maria_ml: Adding that to the patch: case-insensitive compare + map common variants (`yes/no` -> boolean, `true/false`). Also adding a rule: when schema type is `boolean` and model outputs `null`, treat as `false` only if the field is required and we have `default: false` in schema — otherwise keep `null`. That prevents accidental assumptions.

Jenna (ACME): We don't have default for `paid`. For our data model `paid` should always be `false` or `true`, never null. Can you set tenant-level policy to treat required booleans with null -> `false`?

alex_support: We made that tenant policy toggle `coerce_null_booleans_to_false=true` for ACME. Please recheck.

Jenna (ACME): Confirmed: all tests pass. Thanks for the rapid help.

maria_ml: Filed internal issue: ML-2345. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/4821 (parsing fixes + enum normalization). Deploy plan in PR description. We'll follow up with a changelog entry and the SDK patch note (3.0.1) to clarify `strict` behavior.

alex_support: Closing loop: we'll send a summary email + config snapshot and mark as resolved unless you want follow-ups. Also pinging docs to update example prompts. :white_check_mark:

Jenna (ACME): All good, thanks everyone!
